Chashu from heaven
Jan 2019 • Solo
This ramen shop just relocated again, moved to a new place within the Japanese zone. The ramen serves here is shoyu (soy sauce base) ramen. In term of ramen broth, I prefer miso and tonkotsu more. The shoyu broth here taste quite good though. The best thing about ramen here is the chashu; it's excellent, probably the best chashu in town. The chashu melts in your mouth, so tender, juicy and tasty. Five stars for chashu, 3 to 4 stars for everything else. The seasoned boiled egg is a bit salty, probably over seasoning. For a light version of ramen (shoyu and shio), this place is a good choice.

The best ramen in town!
Dec 2017 • Friends
This is the best ramen place in Hochiminh city. As a fan of Japanese cuisine and particularly ramen, I’ve been to many ramen stores but this is by far still the best in my opinion. It’s a quaint little establishment situated in the catacomb of small alley ways connecting Le Thanh Ton street and Thai Van Lung street, it’s like a little Jap town there with myriad of restaurant, massage parlour, bar and shop there.
The noodle here is handmade by the chef, he made a fixed amount everyday so sometimes they might ran out of noodle and will close up shop early. It’s one of the best noodle i’ve had, soft yet firm to the bite, smooth and slippery so you can slurp it up, which is the right way to eat Jap ramen, it’s a compliment to the chef to make slurping sounds. The broth is hearty and fulfilling, you can really taste the bone flavor, not the MSG additives like the broth in many places in Vietnam. There’s only 2 kind of broth, one soy sauce flavor and one tsukemen (dipped ramen with a touch of vinegar in the broth). You can choose the compliment ingredients to go with ramen such as eggs, pork belly meat, bamboo shoot, nori seaweed.....
The only downside of this place is that it’s very small, only enough counter seats for 8-9 people, so you often have to queue til your turn. And it’s not a place for gathering and chit chat, you just go in, eat and then leave. But that’s the way it is, it’s exactly like some ramen store in Japan where they serve ramen for mostly office workers. It’s very space efficient, the whole store is like only 20m2 and they manage to have 8-9 counter seat plus a kitchen for 3 chef/chef de commis.
This is defo a place to frequent if you are a Japanese cuisine lover!

Ramen prepared with care
Mar 2018 • Friends
This is one of those tiny restaurants in the alleys off Le Thanh Ton. There are no tables, just seats at the bar looking at the cooks preparing your Ramen dishes. There may be a queue. 

The ramen comes in two ways: in soup or dry. I took the noodles in the soup with pork and boiled egg and I wasn’t disappointed. The soup itself was a bit salty, but the noodles are perfectly done. The cooks take great care in preparing each component of the dish. I would probably come again to try the dry noodles.
